items.measure: China export licensing for certain graphite items (MOFCOM/GACC Announcement No. 39 of 2023)
items.relevance: Licensing on high-purity/high-strength/high-density synthetic graphite and natural flake graphite products gives Beijing visibility and leverage over graphite leaving China, an incentive to process in third countries.
items.source_name: IEA Policies database (summarising MOFCOM/GACC announcement); corroborated by Mayer Brown and Hogan Lovells (JDSupra)
items.note: Announced 20 Oct 2023, effective 1 Dec 2023. Claim's 'Dec 2023' is the effective date; the announcement date is 20 Oct 2023. No MOFCOM primary page retrieved; secondary sources (IEA, law firms) agree on number, dates and scope.

items.measure: One Big Beautiful Bill Act (Pub. L. 119-21) signed; PFE / material-assistance limits added to 45X, 45Y, 48E
items.relevance: Creates the tax-credit test that makes the ownership and origin of anode material inside US-made batteries financially material, which is what makes rerouting through third-country plants relevant.
items.source_name: IRS Notice 2026-15 (cites Pub. L. 119-21, 139 Stat. 72, July 4, 2025); IRS newsroom; EY Tax News
items.note: Confirmed via IRS primary text. PFE is defined in IRC 7701(a)(51) and material assistance in 7701(a)(52). For 45Y/48E the material-assistance test applies to facilities beginning construction after 31 Dec 2025; for 45X it applies to components sold in tax years beginning after enactment.

items.measure: China announces export controls on lithium-battery and artificial graphite anode items (MOFCOM/GACC Announcement No. 58 of 2025)
items.relevance: Would have extended Chinese licensing from graphite feedstock to anode materials, cells and anode-making equipment and technology, the inputs that third-country anode plants depend on.
items.source_name: Fred Gao (translation of MOFCOM/GACC No. 58/2025); CIRS Group; Global Times
items.note: Issued 9 Oct 2025 with a scheduled effective date of 8 Nov 2025, but suspended before that date (see the 2025-11-07 entry). Not a claim in the original list; added as a newer action.

items.measure: China suspends Announcements No. 55-58, 61, 62 of 2025 until 10 Nov 2026 (MOFCOM/GACC Announcement No. 70 of 2025)
items.relevance: The October 2025 anode/battery controls are paused under the US-China truce; the 2023 graphite licensing (No. 39) stays in force.
items.source_name: CIRS Group; Global Times; Pillsbury; chemradar
items.note: Legal end date of the suspension is 10 Nov 2026. On 28 Sep 2026 MOFCOM said the wider US–China truce runs to 10 Jan 2027, but as of 18 Oct 2026 no new announcement has moved the legal end date. Re-check after 10 Nov 2026.

items.measure: Commerce final affirmative AD/CVD determinations on active anode material from China (A-570-194, C-570-195)
items.relevance: Shows Commerce found Chinese anode material dumped and subsidised at very high rates, which raises the incentive to ship via non-Chinese plants.
items.source_name: ITA (trade.gov) fact sheet; Federal Register 91 FR 7247 (AD, FR Doc. 2026-02998) and 91 FR 7261 (CVD, FR Doc. 2026-02999)
items.note: CORRECTED: announced 11 Feb 2026 but published in the Federal Register on 17 Feb 2026 (both notices 'applicable February 17, 2026'), not around 11 Feb. AD: 93.50% for the separate-rate exporters/producers (including BTR, Shanshan, Zhongke Shinzoom combinations); China-wide entity 102.72%. CVD: 66.82% (Huzhou Kaijin; AFA) and 66.86% (Panasonic Global Procurement China and All Others), so '~66.8%' should read 66.82-66.86%. The final scope excludes AAM incorporated into lithium-ion battery products (per USITC report).

items.measure: IRS Notice 2026-15: interim guidance on material assistance from prohibited foreign entities
items.relevance: Gives the material assistance cost ratio (MACR) method and safe harbors that battery makers use to show their anode inputs are not PFE-sourced. This is where supplier certification of non-Chinese anode origin matters.
items.note: Confirmed. The notice says little on who counts as a PFE or on effective control; proposed regulations are promised. Comments were due 30 Mar 2026. The statute requires PFE safe-harbor tables by 31 Dec 2026 (per McGuireWoods).

items.measure: USITC negative final determinations on active anode material from China (701-TA-752, 731-TA-1730)
items.relevance: Because the Commission voted no, no AD/CVD orders were issued. Chinese anode material avoids those duties, so routing around duties no longer matters, while the PFE tax-credit test still does.
items.note: CORRECTED wording: the finding was that imports have NOT 'materially retarded the establishment of an industry in the United States', not a standard 'no material injury' finding. Vote was 2-1 (Karpel and Johanson negative; Kearns affirmative). Commerce will not issue AD or CVD orders. The FR notice of the determinations was published 3 Apr 2026 (per the FR document list).

items.measure: EVE Energy added to the US Section 1260H list of Chinese military companies
items.relevance: EVE Energy owns the Malaysian cell plant in Case 6. The listing doesn't ban commercial purchases, but it restricts US defense procurement and is a signal buyers screen for.
items.source_name: Federal Register Doc. 2026-11571 (10 Jun 2026); WilmerHale; Holland & Knight
items.note: List published 8 Jun 2026; Federal Register notice dated 10 Jun 2026.

items.measure: MOFCOM says the US–China trade truce runs to 10 Jan 2027
items.relevance: The political deadline for China's paused graphite and battery export controls moves to Jan 2027, but the legal suspension in Announcement 70 still ends on 10 Nov 2026 unless a new announcement is issued.
items.source_name: Global Times (MOFCOM statement); China Briefing; Thomson Reuters

items.measure: Status check: further PFE guidance (proposed regs / safe-harbor tables)
items.relevance: Who counts as a PFE, and the effective-control rules, would determine whether Chinese-owned plants in Indonesia, Morocco or Oman are PFEs.
items.note: Re-checked 18 Oct 2026: still nothing beyond Notice 2026-15. The safe-harbor tables are due by 31 Dec 2026, and questions on effective control and Hong Kong remain open.
